craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as awakening (prabodha); vyabhicāri clarity (prasāda) of transcending. Sanskrit-first: peśala/bhava/madhyākāra opens kept (half-formed/mixed — obscurity marked, not smoothed); prabuddha bhava (AWAKE — BECOME: two imperatives, the verse's only act). Abhinavagupta frame: dream-delusion (svapna) as the accurate ontology of things — clever (peśala) modifies the delusion, not the dreamer. Rows: 9 (past-doubting/fearing/staining/scheming — transcend-list kept whole), 1 (‘become’ end-weighted — the second imperative closes; awakening lands as becoming), 8 (vowel fall: clever-scheming chatter → awake-become stillness). Close: ‘awake — become’. Rupture: the colon before ‘awake’ (delusion inventoried, then the act). Rejected: ‘clever-vs-cunning’ resolved — killed by UNC; ‘planning’ for scheming — killed: scheming schemes (kalpanā contrives); ‘wake up’ — killed: colloquial, prabodha is awakening. Read aloud: PAST non-BE-ing, BE-ing, DO-ing … WHAT-truth COULD they HAVE … PAST-doubt-ing, FEAR-ing, STAIN-ing … a-WAKE — be-COME.

lines: Past non-being, being, doing — things, always, suddenly, in this becoming, half-formed and mixed in change: what truth could they have?
In the untrue, restless, teeming, clever dream-delusion — past doubting, fearing, staining, and reason’s scheming: awake — become.
l4.sanskrit_cite: pūrvābhāvabhavakriyā hi sahasā bhāvāḥ sadā 'smin bhave madhyākāravikārasaṃkaravatāṃ teṣāṃ kutaḥ satyatā | niḥsatye capale prapañcanicaye svapnabhrame peśale śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ prabuddho bhava

reads_against.argmap: Whence the truth of things? → Things lack truth; the only response is awakening: transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning; awaken.
c1_essence: Former non-being, being, action — things always, suddenly here, middle-formed and confused: whence their truth? In the non-true, unsteady, manifold, clever dream-delusion — transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning's contriving: awakened, become. Things lack truth; the only response is awakening.
